To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“A new operating system built for cloud computing can achieve increased efficiency and scale, but it must take into account the deployment of applications in cloud environments.

(i) the cloud is a distributed computing platform, (ii) applications can be deployed as distributed compositions of operating system functionality, and (iii) the cloud can be used to enable innovation in operating systems.

“A new model for distributed application deployment, which we call the Application Operating System (AOS) model, enables operating system innovation by allowing each application to employ its own customized OS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
enabling operating system innovation in the cloud, and our contributions are three-fold. First
enabling operating system innovation in cloud computing.
enabling a more diverse and dynamic ecosystem of OSes in the cloud.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
The cloud computing model is a new way of using computers and information technology that allows users to access computing services and software over a network.
the operating system is no longer the center of the cloud computing universe.
the operating system is no longer the primary software layer that is used to build cloud services and applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the OS should be a service in the cloud.
we are proposing a new model for cloud computing, where applications can use their own operating systems.
we have developed an architecture that allows the cloud to be built on top of a collection of application-driven operating system instances.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cloud is an ideal environment to explore the use of OS compositions, which can be dynamically assembled and customized to the application.
we are not advocating a wholesale replacement of the OS, but rather a new way to think about OS functionality.
the operating system is not a fundamental building block for the cloud.
